newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China partner seeks to dissolve Japan JV golf club.
newsitem.headline: China partner seeks to dissolve Japan JV golf club.

text.p: The Shenzhen Bao Heng (Group) Co Ltd has asked the Chinese government to dissolve its joint venture golf club with a Japanese company because of a tax dispute, the official Securities Times reported on Thursday.

Bao Heng has asked the China International Economic and Foreign Trade Arbitration Commission to end the relationship with the Japanese partner, whose name the newspaper gave in Chinese as the Anle Development Co, the Shenzhen paper said.
The Shenzhen-based Honichi golf club earlier this week held an extraordinary board of directors meeting to discuss the dispute between the two sides, the report said.

The Chinese partner has suggested the joint venture be closed down and its assets turned over to the tax authorities, but the Japanese side has refused to agree, leading to the need for arbitration, it said.

Official Chinese media reports say the dispute stems from the Japanese partner's refusal to remit income from membership fees to Honichi, leaving the joint venture with no funds to pay 95.3 million yuan in taxes and fines.
Representatives of the Japanese side have been quoted by a Hong Kong newspaper as saying there was no need to pay tax to China under the Sino-Japanese Double-Taxation Prevention Treaty.
Chinese authorities have already auctioned off nine cars and frozen the bank account of the club after it failed to pay taxes, a club official said on Wednesday. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
